chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Nu'man, from Bureyd Al-Ajaly, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them,

"That no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve." He (peace be upon him) said: "By Allah! These are our Shiites, when their souls arrive in Paradise and they are welcomed with honor by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, they know and are convinced that they were upon the Truth and upon the Religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, from among the believers, [knowing] that no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve."
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Shiites' referred to in the verse about believers rejoicing in Paradise?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies the believers in Surah Ali 'Imran (3:170) as the Shi'a of the Ahl al-Bayt, highlighting their eschatological joy upon entering Paradise. This narration underscores the Shia belief that the faithful will be assured of their truth and will rejoice for their brethren who follow them, reflecting the promise that 'no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.'
